scope: Primary PostgreSQL 17 technical mechanics; effective-authority fixture is illustrative, not Core P12 implementation.

inspected_points: Privileges are additive through direct grants, memberships and PUBLIC.
A column is writable when UPDATE is held for that column or the whole table; a column-level revoke does not remove a table-level grant.
The unsafe fixture grants table UPDATE then revokes a column, demonstrating why that combination does not protect the field. This PostgreSQL fact is not an implementation of P12.
RLS controls which rows are selected or changed and does not alone impose an arbitrary per-field patch allowlist.
Superusers/BYPASSRLS and ordinarily table owners bypass policies. The command executor is neither a bypass role nor table owner.
Mutable-policy subqueries can race; cooperating writes use a current effective-authority row lock before their source row lock in this fixture.
A row updater/SELECT FOR UPDATE or SHARE waits for another updater, then evaluates the updated row.
Real policy-save and staff-missionary sessions demonstrate lock ordering and source revision checks; no stale browser snapshot is trusted as final authority.
Multiple transactional steps commit together or have no effect after failure.
The source update, required audit and acceptance receipt execute in one SQL transaction. A constraint fault and an injected required-audit fault verify rollback.
The test observes committed rows through fresh SQL sessions; it does not crash/restart the database or qualify hosted durability/recovery.
